label: Emergency Fund Before Debt
summary: The central perspective advocates for building an emergency fund before aggressively paying down credit card debt. This approach ensures financial stability and provides a buffer against unexpected expenses, reducing the need to rely on credit. Establishing even a modest emergency fund can prevent future financial setbacks.
conditions: You have no emergency fund set aside.
You can consistently set aside money each month.
caveats: If you have high-interest debt, you may need to balance your approach.
Building an emergency fund may take time and discipline.

label: High-Interest Debt First
summary: Prioritizing the repayment of high-interest credit card debt is crucial for long-term financial health. This approach saves money by reducing the amount of interest paid over time. It is especially beneficial if you have high-interest debt and can allocate larger payments towards it.
conditions: You have high-interest credit card debt.
You can make larger payments towards your debt.
caveats: Focusing solely on debt repayment may deplete your savings.
It may be easier to pay off lower balance cards for psychological benefits.

label: Balance Savings and Debt Repayment
summary: The central perspective advocates for simultaneously building a small emergency fund while paying down high-interest credit card debt. This approach helps manage liquidity and cash flow, reducing financial risk and interest costs. It emphasizes the importance of finding a personal balance between saving and debt repayment.
conditions: You have no emergency fund yet.
You carry high-interest credit card debt.
caveats: This may not always be the right solution.
Sticking to a plan consistently is essential.
